title: Compact requirements document
description: Editor aid for requirements.yaml: a compact, human-editable requirements format grouped into functional areas, non-functional qualities, deferred scope, and optional project domain sections. Structural only — this schema is not a build gate; see FORMAT.md.
markdownDescription: Compact requirements. Group by `functional.<system_area>.As a <role>, I can.<ID>`, `non_functional.<quality>.<ID>`, or a project domain section. Each requirement value reads `<capability> — so that <value> — acceptance: <observable proof>.` Full spec and per-project vocabulary: **FORMAT.md** and **requirements.vocab.md**.

x-authoring.purpose: Compact requirements a human can hand-edit and an LLM can review. Not enforced. Full rules and per-project vocabulary: FORMAT.md and requirements.vocab.md.
rules: One requirement per line; end with a period; include both `— so that` and `— acceptance:`.
Under a role heading, start with a verb, not `I can`.
IDs are `PREFIX-NN`, stable and unique; never renumber or reuse.
Deferred scope goes under `deferred` with a quoted `"[deferred] PREFIX-NN"` key.

functional.description: Functional requirements grouped by system area, then (recommended) by story role.

non_functional.description: Non-functional requirements grouped by quality attribute.

deferred.description: Explicitly deferred / future requirements grouped by area.

additionalProperties.description: A project-specific domain section (e.g. a data/privacy boundary). Declare it in requirements.vocab.md.

snakeCaseKey.description: A lower snake_case grouping key such as `accounts`, `data_policy`, or `openness_and_governance`.

roleKey.description: A role heading written as a user-story actor plus shared capability prefix. Use `As a ..., I can` so requirement lines can start directly with the capability verb.

requirementId.description: A stable requirement identifier: an uppercase area prefix plus a zero-padded sequence number.

deferredRequirementId.description: A stable requirement identifier for future scope: the normal ID prefixed with `[deferred] `.

requirementText.description: One compact requirement sentence. Recommended shape: `<capability> — so that <value> — acceptance: <observable proof>.` Under a role heading, start with the capability verb because the parent already supplies `As a <role>, I can`.
examples: reset my password from a signed email link — so that a lost password is recoverable without support — acceptance: a used or expired link is rejected and a fresh link succeeds.
public endpoints are rate-limited — so that abuse is constrained — acceptance: repeated abusive requests receive throttled responses.

requirementMap.description: A map of requirement IDs to one-line requirement text. Used under non-functional qualities, domain-section groups, and each role heading.

deferredRequirementMap.description: A map of deferred requirement IDs to one-line requirement text. Used only under the top-level `deferred` section.

functionalArea.description: A system-area section. Recommended: group by role heading (`As a <role>, I can`) whose value is a requirement map. A project that does not use roles may put a requirement map directly.

domainSection.description: A project-specific top-level section: snake_case subgroups whose values are requirement maps, like `non_functional`.
